items.followUp: What is data information in a data communication system?

rubric.why: Identifies what control information does.
rubric.description: Explains that it helps control or manage the transmission of data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its control or management purpose.

rubric.why: Gives examples of control information.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant example, such as source/destination addresses or error-checking information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one relevant example.

modelAnswer: Control information is information added to data to help control or manage its transmission.
It may include source and destination addresses or error-checking information.

items.followUp: What does the rowspan attribute do in an HTML table?

rubric.why: Identifies colspan as an HTML table attribute.
rubric.description: States that colspan is an attribute used in an HTML table cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its context as a table attribute.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of the attribute.
rubric.description: States that it makes a cell extend across multiple columns.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cell spanning columns.

modelAnswer: Colspan is an HTML table-cell attribute.
It makes a cell span across two or more columns.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a main heading and a sub-heading on a web page?

rubric.why: Defines a heading.
rubric.description: Explains that a heading gives the title or main topic of a page or section.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing a heading.

rubric.why: Defines a sub-heading in relation to a heading.
rubric.description: Explains that a sub-heading is a lower-level heading for a part of the main topic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing a sub-heading.

modelAnswer: A heading is the title or main topic of a web page or section.
A sub-heading is a lower-level heading that identifies a smaller part of that topic.

items.followUp: Explain normal, boundary and invalid test data, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains normal test data.
rubric.description: States that normal data is valid, ordinary input expected during normal use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition of normal data.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains boundary or extreme test data.
rubric.description: States that boundary/extreme data tests values at or near the limits of the allowed range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition of boundary or extreme data.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains invalid test data.
rubric.description: States that invalid/abnormal data is outside the permitted input and should be rejected or handled.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition of invalid or abnormal data.

rubric.why: Shows how test data is used.
rubric.description: Explains that test data is entered and the result is checked against the expected result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the checking of test results.

modelAnswer: Normal data is valid, ordinary input that the program is expected to process.
Boundary or extreme data tests values at or near the limits of the allowed range.
Abnormal or invalid data is outside the allowed range or of the wrong type, and should be rejected or handled correctly.
The results produced by each test are compared with the expected results.

items.followUp: Explain four benefits of sharing resources through a computer network.

rubric.why: Identifies hardware resource sharing.
rubric.description: Explains that network users can share hardware, such as printers or storage devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct hardware-sharing need.

rubric.why: Identifies information sharing.
rubric.description: Explains that users can exchange or access shared files and data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct data-sharing need.

rubric.why: Identifies communication as a need for networking.
rubric.description: Explains that a network enables communication between users, for example by email or messaging.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct communication need.

rubric.why: Identifies another practical benefit of a network.
rubric.description: Explains that users can share software or an Internet connection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct additional need.

modelAnswer: Resource sharing: users can share hardware such as printers and storage devices.
Data sharing: users can access and exchange files and information.
Communication: users can communicate through services such as email and messaging.
Sharing services: users can share software or use a common Internet connection.

rubric.why: States the purpose of verification.
rubric.description: Explains that verification checks whether the product is being built according to its specifications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct purpose of verification.

rubric.why: States the purpose of validation.
rubric.description: Explains that validation checks whether the completed product meets the user's needs or intended purpose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct purpose of validation.

modelAnswer: Verification checks whether the product is being built according to its specifications.
Validation checks whether the product meets the user's needs and intended purpose.

items.followUp: What information is recorded in a trace table?

rubric.why: Identifies what a trace table records.
rubric.description: States that a trace table records the changing values of variables during an algorithm's execution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning variable values as the algorithm runs.

rubric.why: Explains the table's use.
rubric.description: States that it follows the algorithm step by step and can record outputs or results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its step-by-step tracing or recording of results.

modelAnswer: A trace table records the values of variables as an algorithm is followed step by step.
It may also record outputs, helping to check the algorithm's results.

items.followUp: How can an algorithm help identify errors before a program is written?

rubric.why: Explains how an algorithm organises a solution.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm sets out the solution as clear, ordered steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the ordered-step structure.

rubric.why: Explains how the algorithm supports problem solving.
rubric.description: States that the steps can be checked or tested to find logical errors before coding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining checking/testing before implementation.

modelAnswer: An algorithm breaks a problem into clear, ordered steps for solving it.
These steps can be checked or tested to find logical errors before writing the program.
